explanation: An optimistic edit, in-flight operation or queued background effect is treated as completed before its recorded completion. Hard reload, immediate execution or checking results too soon can expose old state without proving loss or failure of a completed operation. This covers reviewed unfinished work, not acknowledged-save loss, ordinary navigation discarding valid edits or an effect still absent after completion.
verificationGuidance: Observe the actual completion or acknowledgement, then reread the same object or result after processing settles.
Distinguish visible optimistic state from durable saved state and avoid interrupting a multi-request operation with hard reload.
For background effects verify an eligible recipient and wait for the queue; absence immediately after the triggering action is insufficient.

report.name: Data permission group search leaves unrelated All Users visible
report.summary: Searching permission groups for Administrators reportedly leaves All Users visible until another keyboard interaction.
report.expected: Searching for Administrators filters the group list to Administrators.
report.actual: The report says Administrators and All Users remain visible after typing the query and waiting ten seconds; pressing Ctrl+A or clearing and retyping makes All Users disappear.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and open Data permissions > Groups at /admin/permissions/data/group.
Type Administrators into Search for a group and wait ten seconds.
Inspect whether All Users remains visible, then press Ctrl+A without changing the query or clear and retype it.
report.reason: The agent captured the screenshot before the group search was applied and mistook the unfiltered list for the completed search result. This is a premature observation, not evidence that searching for Administrators returns All Users.

explanation: Declaring parsing, prefill or validation broken because it rejects a plausible but unsupported input syntax or noncanonical representation. General familiarity with URI, quoting or hexadecimal conventions does not override the application’s documented/tested format; correctly formed input must be tested before attributing rejection to the parser.
verificationGuidance: Compare the exact input, including slash counts, delimiters, quoting and accepted character case, with supported syntax.
Test the documented/canonical equivalent and inspect resulting field or saved values before claiming a supported input is rejected.

report.name: SQLite connection-string prefill does not populate the Filename field
report.summary: SQLite connection-string prefill does not populate the Filename field.
report.expected: Entering an accepted SQLite connection string should prefill the fields below, including Filename, per the note 'You can use a connection string to pre-fill the details below'.
report.actual: Both reported SQLite strings (one- and two-slash forms) are rejected with a red "Couldn't use this connection string." message, so Filename stays empty. The form's actual example (jdbc:sqlite:///C:/path/to/database.db, three slashes) fills Filename correctly (control).
reproSteps: Unsaved form only; do not submit a connection attempt. Both tested paths are illustrative and need not exist for client-side prefill.
In Admin > Databases, select Add database and choose SQLite.
Enter jdbc:sqlite:/tmp/DBQA-fixture.sqlite in Connection string (optional) and blur the field.
Observe Filename remains empty. Replace the URI with the reported two-slash form jdbc:sqlite://C:/path/to/database.db and blur.
Observe Filename remains empty again.
report.reason: The SQLite parser intentionally requires sqlite:///; upstream unit and e2e tests cover only that form.

report.name: SQLite connection-string prefill turns an absolute Unix path into a relative one
report.summary: SQLite connection-string prefill turns an absolute Unix path into a relative one.
report.expected: Prefilling the absolute SQLite path should preserve /tmp/qa-does-not-exist/third.sqlite rather than change it to a relative path.
report.actual: Paste jdbc:sqlite:///tmp/x.sqlite (absolute Unix path). Filename becomes tmp/x.sqlite (leading slash dropped) and the form still says pre-filled. The Windows placeholder example and manual entry keep the path correctly (control).
reproSteps: Open Admin > Databases > Add a database and select SQLite.
Enter a unique display name and Filename /tmp/qa-does-not-exist/database.sqlite.
Enter jdbc:sqlite:///tmp/qa-does-not-exist/third.sqlite in Connection string, then click Display name.
Inspect the populated Filename.
report.reason: Works as intended: under the common sqlite:/// convention three slashes give a relative path, and an absolute Unix path needs four slashes (sqlite:////tmp/x), which Metabase prefills correctly.

report.name: Embedding secret key rejects a 64-character uppercase hexadecimal key
report.summary: Embedding secret key rejects a 64-character uppercase hexadecimal key.
report.expected: A valid 256-bit hexadecimal key accepts uppercase A–F, or the form clearly states it requires lowercase and normalizes the equivalent hexadecimal encoding.
report.actual: The 64-uppercase-A key is rejected with an 'Assert failed: Invalid embedding-secret-key! Secret key must be a hexadecimal-encoded 25...' error toast. Refresh restores the prior generated key, although A is a valid hexadecimal digit.
reproSteps: As admin open Admin > Embedding with guest embeds enabled and a generated key.
Replace Embedding secret key with AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA (64 uppercase A characters).
Blur the field.
Observe validation error; refresh the page.
report.reason: Works as intended: the secret-key validation accepts lowercase hexadecimal only; lowercasing the key saves it.

report.name: Spark SQL connection string does not prefill host or port
report.summary: Spark SQL connection string does not prefill host or port.
report.expected: Entering a valid Spark SQL connection string prefills the separate connection fields such as Host and Port.
report.actual: Host and Port remain empty with their default placeholder values after entering the connection string.
reproSteps: As the supplied admin, open Admin > Databases > Add a database.
Select Spark SQL in a fresh unsaved form.
Enter jdbc:sparksql;Server=qa-spark.test;Port=10001;Schema=qa_schema in Connection string (optional).
Click Display name and inspect Host and Port.
report.reason: Works as intended: the reported jdbc:sparksql; string doesn't match the documented format, and the form says it couldn't use the string. A string in the documented format pre-fills Host.

explanation: Treating an encoded field representation as corrupted connection data without checking how the server consumes it. Encoding visible in a form can be the required working representation, and decoding it prematurely can change literal percent-containing values.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the value sent to the server and the server-side decode/connection behavior.
Distinguish cosmetic encoded text from a failed connection or a demonstrably altered database identifier.

report.name: PostgreSQL URI prefill keeps percent-encoded database name instead of decoding it
report.summary: PostgreSQL URI prefill keeps percent-encoded database name instead of decoding it.
report.expected: URI prefill should decode dbqa%20test to the database name 'dbqa test', just as it decodes dbqa%40user to dbqa@user.
report.actual: Paste a PostgreSQL URI with a percent-encoded database name (…/dbqa%20test). Database name and the auto display name keep the literal %20, while username, password and query params are decoded. Unencoded names fill correctly (control).
reproSteps: As Admin, open Databases > Add database and select PostgreSQL.
Enter postgresql://dbqa%40user:p%40ss%3Aword@dbqa.invalid:5433/dbqa%20test?sslmode=verify-full in Connection string (optional) and blur.
Read the Database name and Username inputs.
report.reason: The encoded database name is the working form: the server decodes it, so the connection succeeds. Only the displayed field text keeps %20, and decoding in the form could break names that contain a literal percent sign.

explanation: Assuming an administrator-authored URL, domain, template or reusable code field must reject every value that seems malformed or unusable. These fields may deliberately accept relative links, templates, partial code or unconstrained text; saving user-provided content alone does not demonstrate a broken feature. This does not excuse corruption of valid input or an application-generated invalid value.
verificationGuidance: Establish the documented accepted syntax and whether relative paths, templates or partial content are allowed.
Test valid configured content separately from an unusable value deliberately entered by the author.
Show a violated supported contract or concrete unintended effect rather than relying only on the absence of preferred validation.

report.name: Map tile server URL accepts and saves not-a-url
report.summary: Map tile server URL accepts and saves not-a-url.
report.expected: A value that is not a URL is rejected with a validation message.
report.actual: not-a-url saves with Changes saved and persists after reload; pin maps then show no basemap.
reproSteps: As an admin, open Admin > Settings > Maps.
Replace Map tile server URL with not-a-url and move focus away.
Observe Changes saved and reload.
report.reason: Works as intended: the setting has no validation, and the docs allow a relative path as well as an http(s) URL, so not-a-url is a legal value. A well-formed but unreachable URL breaks the map the same way.

report.name: Webhook destinations accept API-key authentication with an empty key and value
report.summary: Webhook destinations accept API-key authentication with an empty key and value.
report.expected: Selecting API Key authentication should require a nonempty key and value before creating or saving the destination.
report.actual: Create destination succeeds with API Key and Header selected but empty Key and Value. Reloading and reopening the destination retains this incomplete configuration. Clearing previously populated Key/Value and saving is also accepted. No delivery failure is claimed.
reproSteps: Sign in as administrator and open /admin/settings/notifications.
Click Add a webhook (or Add another).
Enter https://example.test/qa-webhook as Webhook URL, QA Blank Auth as name, and QA description as Description.
Select API Key authentication and keep Header selected. Leave both Key and Value blank.
Click Create destination.
Reload the settings page and reopen QA Blank Auth. API Key/Header remains selected with empty Key and Value.
report.reason: Works as intended: nothing documents or requires API-key webhook auth to have a non-empty key and value.

report.name: Webhook URL accepts and persists an FTP destination without validation
report.summary: Webhook URL accepts and persists an FTP destination without validation.
report.expected: Saving should be rejected and the form should show "Please enter a correctly formatted URL", because only http: and https: webhook URLs are allowed.
report.actual: The modal closed after Save changes and no error appeared. After a refresh, reopening "Edit this webhook" showed the Webhook URL as ftp://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts.
reproSteps: Sign in as an admin and open /admin/settings/notifications
Click Add a webhook. Enter URL https://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts, name 'QA FTP check 7731' and description 'ftp repro 7731'. Keep Authentication method set to None and click Create destination.
Click the new webhook card to open 'Edit this webhook'. Change Webhook URL to ftp://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts and click Save changes. The modal closes with no error.
Refresh the page and click the webhook card again. Webhook URL shows ftp://qa-webhook.invalid/alerts.
report.reason: Works as intended: the webhook URL field accepts any well-formed URL; an unusable scheme is the admin's input choice.

report.name: Google authentication accepts a URL as an email domain
report.summary: Google authentication accepts a URL as an email domain.
report.expected: Reject a scheme/path URL as invalid for the email-domain field and retain the form for correction.
report.actual: Save displays Success, then reload retains https://invalid-domain/path.
reproSteps: Temporary provider configuration is authorized only while preserving password login and all account credentials. Restore Google to unconfigured immediately via Authentication Overview > Google menu > Deactivate > confirm; this clears client/domain.
As Admin open Authentication > Google auth with provider unconfigured.
Enter syntactically accepted Client ID qa-maps-auth.apps.googleusercontent.com.
Enter https://invalid-domain/path in Domain and click Save and enable.
Observe Success then reload and inspect Domain.
report.reason: Works as intended: the Google sign-in domain is a plain admin-entered value with no documented format; saving it as typed is not broken behavior.

explanation: Reporting an unmasked credential input as a confirmed product defect without a requirement that this particular field mask its contents. Visible text in an authorized configuration form alone does not establish unintended disclosure to another actor.
verificationGuidance: Check the field’s documented behavior and applicable labeling requirements.
If alleging disclosure, demonstrate an unauthorized viewer or unintended exposure beyond the authorized input itself.

report.name: Webhook Basic authentication password is shown in plain text
report.summary: Webhook Basic authentication password is shown in plain text.
report.expected: The webhook Password field masks the entered secret.
report.actual: Typing into the Basic authentication Password field shows the password as readable text.
reproSteps: As an admin, open Admin > Settings > Notifications and add a webhook.
Select Basic authentication.
Type a password and observe it is readable.
report.reason: Works as intended: nothing requires the webhook password field to be masked.

explanation: Correct rejection of invalid input is called a functional defect solely because the reporter prefers more specific wording, another message or an additional error outline. In these reviewed cases valid corrections work, saved values remain intact and the requested extra feedback is not an established requirement. This does not dismiss proven silent refusal, misleading success, an applicable accessibility requirement or missing recovery.
verificationGuidance: Verify whether invalid input is rejected, valid input works and the previous saved state survives.
Identify the applicable feedback contract rather than treating a preferred phrase or extra visual treatment as mandatory.
Separate wording preferences from an independently demonstrated missing-error, misleading-success or recovery defect.

report.name: Whitespace-only group rename opens a generic error dialog
report.summary: Whitespace-only group rename opens a generic error dialog.
report.expected: A whitespace-only group name is rejected with field validation, as an empty name is.
report.actual: Done is enabled for three spaces; clicking it opens a generic Something went wrong dialog. The original name is kept.
reproSteps: As an admin, open Admin > People > Groups and create a group.
Choose Edit Name, enter three spaces, and click Done.
Observe the generic error dialog.
report.reason: Works as intended for labeling purposes: the server rejects the blank name and the original name is kept; specific validation copy here is not a hard requirement.

report.name: Long group names display a raw database error
report.summary: Long group names display a raw database error.
report.expected: A user-friendly validation error message explains the group name length limit without exposing internal database errors.
report.actual: A dialog displays raw SQL exception details: 'Value too long for column "NAME CHARACTER VARYING(255)": ... (295)"; SQL statement: UPDATE "PERMISSIONS_GROUP" SET "NAME" = ? WHERE "ID" = ? [22001-214]'.
reproSteps: As Harbor Admin, create a uniquely named PeopleQA-Groups fixture.
Open its ellipsis > Edit Name.
Enter PeopleQA-Groups-Edge-5329 followed by ten repetitions of -ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ (295 characters total).
Click Done.
report.reason: Works as intended: an overlong group name is rejected and the original name is kept, as with admin-030; specific validation wording is not required.

explanation: An intended action is blamed for a failure even though the recorded input did not activate that action: it reached another element, used an incomplete gesture or editing mode, or simulated a different keyboard shortcut. A tool timeout, surrounding-cell click or value entered into a popup does not establish failure of the intended application control.
verificationGuidance: Confirm the actual event target, focus, editing mode and completed gesture from the rendered UI or recording.
Repeat using the precise anchor, input, drag threshold or real keyboard shortcut; check key and modifier details for simulated events.
Verify the intended control actually ran before attributing navigation failure or value loss to it.

report.name: Accounts Email selection leaves ID metadata in settings panel
report.summary: Selecting Email in Accounts updates the field route to /field/24, but the settings panel remains populated with ID metadata after settling and a repeated selection.
report.expected: After selecting Email in Accounts, the settings panel should show Email and that field’s metadata/settings, consistent with the page’s instruction to select a field to edit its settings.
report.actual: The Email card became highlighted and the URL changed to /admin/datamodel/database/1/schema/1:PUBLIC/table/6/field/24, but the right panel continued to show ID as the field name, BIGINT as its data type, and Entity Key as its semantic type. This remained visible after waiting six seconds and after repeating the ID-to-Email selection.
reproSteps: Authenticate as the Harbor account by loading the supplied saved authentication state.
Navigate to /admin/datamodel/database.
Expand Sample Database in the left sidebar and select Accounts.
Select the ID field and verify the panel shows ID, BIGINT, and Entity Key.
Select Email in the Accounts field list.

Observe the Email card and the URL /admin/datamodel/database/1/schema/1:PUBLIC/table/6/field/24. The right-side panel still shows ID, BIGINT, and Entity Key after waiting six seconds; repeat selecting ID and then Email to confirm the mismatch persists.
report.reason: Selecting Email's field card navigates to field/62 and shows EMAIL and CHARACTER VARYING, including after repeating ID then Email. Clicking its editable name instead does not select field details; field/24 is ID.

explanation: The reviewer labels the reported expectation as intended behavior but records no supporting rationale. These instances are an explicit holding group: the narrow rejection is known, while the specific model reasoning error, source semantics and general product policy are not established.
verificationGuidance: Preserve the exact rejected claim and human decision without inventing a causal explanation.
Do not use this holding group to dismiss a similar new report without checking its own trigger, contract and evidence.
Recover the missing review rationale before assigning the instance to a more specific reasoning-error pattern.

report.name: Clearing table display name and saving silently discards the change and closes the editor
report.summary: Clearing table display name and saving silently discards the change and closes the editor.
report.expected: An invalid empty name should be rejected with clear validation, or an allowed clearing should be stored/reset explicitly; Save should not silently discard the input.
report.actual: After submitting an empty name, the editor closed and retained QA Reference Release Requests. Reload and reopening Edit still showed the prior name. A full-page AI assertion confirmed no validation error or warning was shown.
reproSteps: Open Release operations, Tables in Release operations, and Release Requests.
Edit the table, set its display name to a distinct nonempty QA name and save; verify it persists.
Edit again, clear the display name completely, and click Save.
Observe the editor closes showing the prior name. Reload and reopen Edit.
report.reason: Works as intended per human review.

report.name: Iframe allowed-domain setting saves the invalid hostname “not a domain”
report.summary: Iframe allowed-domain setting saves the invalid hostname “not a domain”.
report.expected: A setting for allowed domains should reject hostnames containing spaces and explain the invalid entry instead of saving it as a usable domain.
report.actual: The literal not a domain is accepted with Changes saved and remains after refresh.
reproSteps: As an admin, note the current Allowed domains for iframes in dashboards so you can restore it afterwards.
Open Admin > Settings > General and scroll to Tables, X-Rays and domains.
Replace Allowed domains for iframes in dashboards with not a domain and blur.
Observe Changes saved; refresh General and inspect the saved domain list.
report.reason: Works as intended per human review.

report.name: Separator style reverts from “100.000,00” to “100,000.00” after refresh
report.summary: Separator style reverts from “100.000,00” to “100,000.00” after refresh.
report.expected: The saved 100.000,00 separator format should remain selected after refresh.
report.actual: The dropdown initially changes to 100.000,00 and shows Changes saved, but after refresh it displays 100,000.00 again.
reproSteps: Open Admin > Settings > Localization.
Scroll to Numbers and open Separator style.
Choose 100.000,00; observe selected format and Changes saved.
Refresh and scroll back to Numbers.
report.reason: Works as intended per human review.

report.name: Entering nonnumeric text in Price multiplier silently deletes the saved multiplier
report.summary: Entering nonnumeric text in Price multiplier silently deletes the saved multiplier.
report.expected: Reject nonnumeric multiplier with validation feedback, retaining the previous saved multiplier rather than saving an empty reset.
report.actual: Entering nonnumeric text leaves the multiplier input empty; on blur, the saved -1.25 multiplier is cleared with a 'Formatting of Price updated' toast, preview values revert from negative (-36.83) to positive (29.46), and the reset persists across a page reload without any validation error.
reproSteps: As admin, open Sample Database > Products > Price in Table Metadata.
Open Preview; scroll field settings to Multiply by a number.
Enter -1.25 and blur; refresh and reopen preview to verify saved negative values such as -36.83.
Replace multiplier with abc and press Tab.
Observe emptied multiplier and original positive preview values; refresh and reopen preview.
report.reason: Works as intended per human review.

explanation: Failure of an author-created incompatible or invalid configuration is reported as failure of a supported valid workflow. The reviewed errors are recoverable or the invalid draft is blocked at normal activation; allowing configuration or Test to expose that error does not establish a guarantee to prevalidate every combination. This does not excuse corrupting a valid definition or losing unrelated saved data.
verificationGuidance: Repair the invalid value, reference, relation or duplicate name and run a valid positive control.
Read the actual validation or execution error and distinguish invalid-draft testing from the normally activated supported flow.
Establish any promised earlier validation stage rather than inferring it from the ability to edit or save configuration.

report.name: A segment can be saved referencing itself, making Preview fail with a recursive-definition error
report.summary: A segment can be saved referencing itself, making Preview fail with a recursive-definition error.
report.expected: The editor should prevent selecting or saving a circular self-reference, with actionable validation rather than saving an unusable definition.
report.actual: The segment saves and retains its own name as a filter. Preview fails with 'There was a problem with your question' and 'Segment expansion failed. Check mutually recursive segment definitions.'
reproSteps: Use disposable SEG-QA segments on Sample Database / People. Observed second fixture was SEG-QA-Dependent-20261019 and referenced retired SEG-QA-People-20261019-v2 before adding itself. Its preview worked immediately before adding the self-reference.
Create a disposable People segment filtered to State CA.

Create a second disposable segment referencing the first; verify Preview returns 90 rows. In the observed setup the first segment was subsequently retired, and the second still previewed successfully.
Edit the second segment, click Add filter and select that same second segment as an additional filter.
Enter a change reason and click Save changes. Reopen the segment and click Preview.
Open Show error details.
report.reason: Works as intended per human review: saving is allowed and Preview explains the recursive definition.

report.name: Presto Kerberos authentication rejects its own principal property as not allowed
report.summary: Presto Kerberos authentication rejects its own principal property as not allowed.
report.expected: The offered Kerberos principal input should be supported; unavailable credentials or host can produce an appropriate authentication/connection failure.
report.actual: Save fails with 'Connection property KerberosPrincipal is not allowed' rather than accepting the form's own principal property.
reproSteps: Open Add database > Presto; enter host qa.invalid, port8080, catalog mo_catalog, schema mo_schema, username mo_qa and a display name.
Enable Authenticate with Kerberos under advanced options.
Enter Kerberos principal mo_qa@QA.INVALID and cache-file path /tmp/mo-qa-missing-cache.
Save.
report.reason: Works as intended: Presto requires the Kerberos coordinator service for Kerberos auth. The form does not mark required fields and the placeholder is an example, so the rejection of an incomplete config is driver validation with imprecise wording.

report.name: Saving an indirect segment cycle A→B→A breaks the previously working dependent segment B
report.summary: Saving an indirect segment cycle A→B→A breaks the previously working dependent segment B.
report.expected: Reject the edit that introduces a circular dependency, keeping the existing dependent segment B usable.
report.actual: A saves successfully referencing B while B references A. Preview displays 'There was a problem with your question' and 0 rows. Neither segment directly references itself.
reproSteps: As Admin create a fresh SegQA-prefixed segment A on Sample Database Products with Category is Gadget; enter name/description after choosing filter, save.
Create segment B on Products filtered only by A; save and reopen B to verify 53 rows.
Open A and add B as another filter; supply a revision reason and Save changes.
Reopen B, whose definition has not changed, and click Preview; switch to the newly opened tab.
report.reason: Works as intended for labeling: consistent with data-modeling-146, saving a recursive segment definition is allowed and the query error names the recursive definition.

explanation: Assuming replacing a connection string resets every existing field even when the new string supplies no replacement for that field. Prefill can intentionally update only supplied values; retaining a visibly populated port omitted from the new string is not proof of stale parsing.
verificationGuidance: Check whether prefill is a partial update or full replacement by contract.
Compare supplied properties with the existing field values, and test an explicit replacement value separately.

report.name: Replacing MySQL connection string with one omitting port retains previous custom port 3307
report.summary: Replacing MySQL connection string with one omitting port retains previous custom port 3307.
report.expected: When replacing the connection string with one that omits the port, the Port field should clear or revert to the default (3306) rather than retaining the previous custom port.
report.actual: Host, database name, and username update to match the new connection string, but the Port field remains filled with 3307 from the previous connection string.
reproSteps: Open Admin > Databases > Add database and select MySQL.
Enter jdbc:mysql://qa_user:qa_pass@db.example.test:3307/qa_db?ssl=true and blur.
Confirm fields show host db.example.test and port 3307.
Replace the URI with jdbc:mysql://qa_second:second_pass@second.example.test/second_db and blur.
Inspect host, database, username and Port.
report.reason: Works as intended: connection-string prefill only fills fields the string provides; upstream e2e tests assert a portless string keeps the existing Port.

explanation: Failure caused by an incorrect public instance URL or reverse-proxy scheme configuration is attributed to application behavior under a valid deployment. Wrong origins can make generated links unreachable, and missing original-scheme forwarding can create redirect loops. A product defect requires evidence that the correctly configured supported environment still fails.
verificationGuidance: Verify the configured external URL, actual browser origin and required proxy forwarding headers.
Repeat with the supported configuration and inspect fresh requests, not only a page already affected by redirects.
Do not generalize an environment-specific rejection to incorrect application-generated links under valid configuration.

report.name: Enabling Redirect to HTTPS locks the HTTPS site in a redirect loop
report.summary: Enabling Redirect to HTTPS locks the HTTPS site in a redirect loop.
report.expected: Already-HTTPS requests should load normally after enabling HTTPS redirects. Only HTTP requests should redirect to HTTPS.
report.actual: Immediately after enabling the switch at 16:59:22 UTC, fresh HTTPS Admin navigations failed in multiple browser sessions with ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS. Network evidence shows repeated HTTP 301 responses whose Location is the exact same HTTPS request URL (for example /admin/settings/general?qa-recovery=1). A new query string also loops. The setting was restored with a narrow cleanup PUT false from a still-open page; cached permanent redirects also needed refreshing.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator at / and open /admin/settings/general. Ensure Redirect to HTTPS starts Disabled.
Enable Redirect to HTTPS and wait for Changes saved.
Open /admin/settings/general in a fresh tab or reload the HTTPS page.
Observe the browser's ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS error. Inspect the network: HTTPS requests receive 301 redirects to their identical HTTPS URLs.
report.reason: Fixture issue: the sandbox proxy terminates TLS without forwarding the original scheme, so Metabase sees every request as HTTP and redirects. With a correct proxy header the same requests succeed.

report.name: Discarding an unsaved PostgreSQL connection form opens 'Something’s gone wrong' instead of the database list
report.summary: Discarding an unsaved PostgreSQL connection form opens 'Something’s gone wrong' instead of the database list.
report.expected: Discard the new unsaved connection and return to the working database list.
report.actual: Database list route displays 'Something’s gone wrong' with refresh/back advice. Show error details displays only 'An error occurred'.
reproSteps: No database was created. URLs are disposable test values, not working credentials. Exact relevance of the encoded URL or advanced options to this failure is uncertain.
Open Admin > Databases > Add database (PostgreSQL).
Enter disposable connection string postgresql://qa_user:qa_demo@localhost:5432/qa_connection and blur.
Replace it with postgresql://qa%40user:demo%40pass@localhost:5433/qa%20connection?sslmode=require and blur.
Scroll down, expand Show advanced options, and verify JDBC options show sslmode=require.
Click Cancel, then Discard changes in the confirmation dialog.
report.reason: Cannot reproduce: the original run overlapped another agent enabling Redirect to HTTPS behind the sandbox proxy, so every API call returned 301; discarding the form returns to the database list normally.

report.name: Saving a new Sample Database Orders question in Our analytics shows “An error occurred”
report.summary: Saving a new Sample Database Orders question in Our analytics shows “An error occurred”.
report.expected: The new question is saved in the selected collection.
report.actual: Save dialog stays open and displays “An error occurred”; assertion saw submit button temporarily labeled “Failed”. Question creation could not complete.
reproSteps: As Admin, exit Admin, use New > Dashboard to create and save an empty disposable dashboard in Our analytics (used only as prerequisite context).
Use New > Question, choose Sample Database > Orders, then click Save in notebook editor.
Enter a fresh question name.
Change save location from Release overview to Our analytics using location picker > Browse > Our analytics > Select this collection.
Click Save.
report.reason: Cannot reproduce: the original run overlapped another agent enabling Redirect to HTTPS behind the sandbox proxy, so follow-up API calls returned 301s; the same flow works normally.

report.name: Saving a People segment with Source Is not Google/Facebook opens 'An error occurred' instead of the Segments list
report.summary: Saving a People segment with Source Is not Google/Facebook opens 'An error occurred' instead of the Segments list.
report.expected: Saving the valid exclusion segment returns to a usable list showing the new definition.

reproSteps: As admin open Table Metadata > Segments > New segment.
Select Sample Database > People. Add Source Is Google, enter a unique name and description, and Save changes.
Reopen the segment; open Source filter, search Face, select Facebook as well, and Update filter.
Enter reason for changes and Save changes. Reopen segment and verify Google and Facebook selected with 1015 rows.
Open Source filter > operator Is > Is not > Update filter. The editor shows 1485 rows.
Enter reason QA exclude two sources and Save changes.
Inspect destination Segments list.
report.reason: Cannot reproduce: the original run overlapped another agent enabling Redirect to HTTPS behind the sandbox proxy, so follow-up API calls returned 301s; the same flow works normally.

explanation: Assuming duplicate-name validation must trim meaningful whitespace because two distinct stored names look the same when rendered. If spaces are permitted in names, a trailing space can intentionally distinguish them; visual similarity alone does not establish a duplicate-key bypass.
verificationGuidance: Compare the exact stored strings and the documented normalization/uniqueness rule.
Demonstrate rejection requirements for whitespace-padded variants rather than assuming trimming is mandatory.

report.name: Trailing space bypasses webhook duplicate-name validation and creates identical-looking channel names
report.summary: Trailing space bypasses webhook duplicate-name validation and creates identical-looking channel names.
report.expected: Duplicate-name protection should treat visually identical names consistently, rejecting or normalizing whitespace padding.

explanation: A technical observation is submitted as an eligible benchmark bug without checking the benchmark's accepted scope. Recorded exclusions include accessibility-only claims with no accepted visible or pointer defect, API-only states unavailable through supported UI, and explicitly excluded exotic inputs. A scope exclusion does not prove the underlying technical issue cannot exist.
verificationGuidance: Read the applicable benchmark eligibility rule and the exact recorded exclusion.
Establish the supported UI path, input domain and accepted observable impact for the new claim.
Evaluate a separately demonstrated functional failure independently; do not convert an exclusion into a universal product-correctness claim.

report.name: Map property choices all have the accessible name “[object Object]”
report.summary: Map property choices all have the accessible name “[object Object]”.

report.actual: After loading a valid GeoJSON, the accessibility snapshot shows all three choices as option “[object Object]”. reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and open /admin/settings/maps.
Click Add a map.
Enter any map name and set the GeoJSON URL to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datasets/geo-countries/master/data/countries.geojson, then click Load.
Open “Which property specifies the region's identifier?” using a screen reader or inspect the browser accessibility tree.
Observe that name, ISO3166-1-Alpha-3, and ISO3166-1-Alpha-2 are all announced/exposed as “[object Object]”. The region display-name selector has the same issue.
report.reason: Not a product bug for labeling: the defect exists only in the accessibility tree and nothing visible or functional is broken.

report.name: Custom field ordering ignores its advertised keyboard controls

report.actual: With Created At focused, trusted Space, ArrowUp, Space key events reach the sortable button, but data-is-dragging remains false and the order stays ID, Region, Category, Approved, Amount, Created At. reproSteps: As admin, open Admin → Table Metadata → Release operations → Release Requests (/admin/datamodel/database/2/schema/2:public/table/9).
Click Sorting, then select Custom order.
Use Tab to focus the Created At sortable field button. It is the last field in the original database order; its accessible description instructs Space to pick up and arrow keys to move.
Press Space, ArrowUp, then Space.

report.reason: Not a product bug for labeling: the missing keyboard reorder is an accessibility-only issue with no visible or pointer-driven defect.

explanation: Expecting a public execution page to expose detailed internal errors or preserve an editable retry form when it deliberately uses a generic error screen. In the reviewed case the author also supplied a read query to a write-action executor; the generic public error does not establish a valid action failed.
verificationGuidance: Confirm the action is valid for its executor before evaluating the public result.
Compare public error-disclosure behavior with the intended public/private boundary and test the same action in an authorized editor.

explanation: A visible input transformation is attributed to silent save-time corruption even though the field or preview already shows the effective value before submission. Reviewed controls normalize unsupported characters, dates or precision; saving that displayed accepted value is different from secretly replacing a valid submitted value.
verificationGuidance: Record the input and preview immediately before blur, Apply or Save, then compare the submitted and persisted values.
Check the field-specific normalization contract and a supported-input control.
Do not use this rejection to dismiss hidden value substitution or corruption that first occurs during a completed save.

explanation: The claimed missing, changed or unusable state is contradicted by a decisive observation or controlled verification of that same claim. Examples include an allegedly lost value remaining intact or an allegedly broken action succeeding under the stated setup. This disproves the checked allegation, not every related workflow or the possibility of a different historical failure.
verificationGuidance: Verify the actual displayed, submitted and persisted values, and the precise action target, instead of repeating the original interpretation.
Repeat the reported setup and a positive control; record what the decisive observation actually establishes.
Keep any different trigger, transient state or accepted neighboring defect separate from the contradicted claim.

explanation: Arbitrary integers beyond the browser's safe numeric representation are assumed to round-trip exactly without an established exact-integer guarantee. Rounding outside that range does not demonstrate corruption of ordinary supported values. An explicit precision promise or a failure within the supported range requires separate assessment.
verificationGuidance: Check the field's supported range and representation, including the safe-integer boundary where relevant.
Compare the value during entry, the submitted payload and the stored result; a final screenshot alone does not establish when rounding occurred.
Use ordinary in-range controls and preserve any explicit exact-precision requirement.

explanation: Fractional input is treated as supported precision in a control whose reviewed contract represents integer counts, offsets or raw units. Conversion or rejection of a fraction does not establish loss of supported data, and a preferred warning policy is not automatically required. Valid integer corruption and fields promising fractional precision remain separate.
verificationGuidance: Determine the stored unit and supported numeric domain, not just whether the input accepts decimal keystrokes.
Test valid integer controls and inspect the effective value before and after submission.
Establish an explicit fractional-precision or warning contract before treating normalization as a defect.

explanation: A stale editor is expected to merge another writer's changes or warn about conflicts even though the reviewed contract accepts last-write-wins saves. A full stale-object submission can restore its displayed fields without establishing corruption of the submitted data. This ruling does not cover a promised merge guarantee or loss without a competing write.
verificationGuidance: Check the documented or adjudicated concurrency contract before requiring automatic merging or conflict detection.
Inspect both editors' saved baselines and submitted fields, then repeat without another writer.
Distinguish an accepted stale full-object save from a completed value disappearing without an intervening write.

explanation: Assuming access to a visible base table is sufficient for a query that also resolves foreign-key display names through other tables. The apparent single-table result can require implicit joins and therefore permissions on those related tables.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the generated query, remapping and implicit joins.
Compare permissions for every required table, and test without display remapping before alleging a base-table permission failure.

explanation: Content outside the initially visible portion of a scrollable menu, panel or narrow input is assumed absent, incorrect or unusable. In the reviewed cases scrolling or copying reveals the complete value and the control works. This does not cover essential content that remains inaccessible through normal supported interaction.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the full scroll container and input value, including content above or beyond the initial viewport.
Use normal scrolling, text navigation or copying to verify the complete value and the selectable control.
Retest the actual task after revealing the content; preserve a claim if normal access still fails.

explanation: A reported failure is treated as established without recovering the claimed failing state after independent review could not reproduce it. Nonreproduction leaves the historical event and its cause unresolved; it does not prove the behavior impossible or intended, and a nearby accepted bug does not verify a different trigger or outcome.
verificationGuidance: Reproduce the exact reported trigger and outcome in a fresh, isolated state, with the required permissions and completed saves.
Keep an unrecovered historical claim explicitly unverified; do not invent an intended-behavior or source-cause explanation.
Compare the exact claim with accepted nearby cases rather than borrowing their evidence.

report.summary: Negative decimal places crashes table and field metadata panes.

Scroll to Number of decimal places. Enter 3, then open Preview to verify a value such as 120.000.
Close Preview, scroll back to Number of decimal places, and replace 3 with -1.

explanation: An edited local value is assumed saved without establishing that the supported commit action ran. Enter, synthetic blur and an open editor do not universally mean the rename or form was submitted; reload restoring the old value does not prove a completed save was lost.
verificationGuidance: Use the actual supported commit gesture for this editor and verify its completion or persistence acknowledgement.
Compare trusted outside-click, Enter, Tab or explicit Save controls as applicable; do not assume a programmatic event is equivalent.
Reopen or reread the same object after the confirmed commit before claiming saved-value loss.

report.name: Table rename is not saved when pressing Enter and reverts after reload
report.summary: Table rename is not saved when pressing Enter and reverts after reload.
report.expected: Pressing Enter to submit a new table name should save and persist the change after reload.
report.actual: Pressing Enter does not update the sidebar or save the table name; upon page reload, the name reverts to the previous name ('QA-TABLE Reviews').
reproSteps: As an admin, open Admin > Table Metadata > Sample Database > Reviews.
Rename the table to QA-TABLE Reviews and click outside the input; reload to verify this baseline persists.
Change the table name to QA-TABLE Reviews café & <sample> and press Enter.
Observe that the header and sidebar keep the old name, then reload: the name reverts to QA-TABLE Reviews.
report.reason: Works as intended: the table-name input saves on blur, not on Enter, and the documented save action (clicking away) persists the name. Pressing Enter just leaves an unsaved draft in the focused input.

explanation: Temporary interactive state is assumed to be a saved setting that must survive refresh or preview regeneration. A contextual list filter can require an explicit saved view, while an embedding preview can reload its configured initial values when its token changes. Loss of these unsaved runtime choices is distinct from loss of completed saved settings.
verificationGuidance: Identify whether the value belongs to a saved view/default or only the current navigation or preview session.
Use the supported save or initial-value configuration, then verify that persisted setting survives the same transition.
Keep initial navigation using the wrong context and completed saved settings being lost as separate claims.

report.name: Changing a locked preview parameter clears the editable grouping
report.summary: Changing a locked preview parameter clears the editable grouping.
report.expected: Applying a locked Date Range preview value preserves the independently selected Year grouping on the dashboard.
report.actual: Date Grouping loses the selected Year value and resets to default, causing the chart to revert from yearly to quarterly labels.
reproSteps: As admin open Embedding settings and enable guest embeds if disabled.
Set Date Range to Locked and Date Grouping to Editable.
In dashboard preview choose Date Grouping > Year. Observe year labels 2025 and 2026.
In Previewing locked parameters choose Date Range > Previous 12 months.
Observe Date Grouping loses Year and chart displays Q4 2025 through Q3 2026.
report.reason: Works as intended: changing a locked parameter regenerates the signed preview token, which reloads the preview from its configured initial values. Setting the grouping as an initial parameter value keeps it, so nothing is broken.

explanation: Assuming invalid or blank input must remain as an error instead of reverting to the previous valid value, being treated as no value, or being constrained to a supported minimum. The reviewed controls deliberately use fallback/clearing behavior; showing a different parsed condition alone does not establish data corruption. This does not cover a valid accepted value that is secretly replaced.
verificationGuidance: Identify the control’s documented/tested invalid-input and blank-input policy.
Inspect the retained calendar selection, range bounds and applied chip rather than only transient typed text.
Test a supported valid value and verify it is preserved before inferring a general save failure.

report.name: Zero-day relative date filter silently saves as one day
report.summary: Zero-day relative date filter silently saves as one day.
report.expected: Reject an unsupported zero-day interval with validation, or preserve the explicitly entered interval instead of silently changing it.
report.actual: Zero is accepted without validation. The saved list says Birth Date is yesterday; reopening the picker shows Previous 1 day, silently changing the input from 0 to 1.
reproSteps: Create a disposable People segment with State is CA, unique name and description; save.
Edit it and add Birth Date > Relative date range.
Leave Previous selected, replace interval 30 with 0, keep day and Include today off.
Click Add filter, enter revision reason, Save changes and refresh.
Reopen the segment and click the Birth Date filter chip.
report.reason: Works as intended: a relative date interval must be at least 1, so 0 days is saved as 1 day (same as querying-367).

explanation: Treating an input’s placeholder as a real default and reporting validation failure when a required field was never filled. A displayed example port does not mean that port is in the submitted configuration.
verificationGuidance: Read the input value attribute or submitted payload rather than its placeholder text.
Explicitly enter the required value and retry the same configuration.

report.name: MongoDB SSH form shows an integer port assertion error
report.expected: The default ports should be usable, or the form should identify a required port value with actionable validation.
report.actual: The connection alert reads “Assert failed: (integer? port)” rather than a usable connection or validation message.
reproSteps: Open Add database as admin, select MongoDB and set a display name.
Choose Use a connection string and enter mongodb://qa-connection.invalid:27017/qa_mongo?connectTimeoutMS=1000&serverSelectionTimeoutMS=1000.
Enable SSH tunnel, use qa-ssh.invalid, username qa_ssh, Password authentication and dummy password qa_dummy_password; leave SSH port at displayed 22.
Switch to Fill out host, port and database name.
Enter Host qa-connection.invalid and Database name qa_mongo, leave MongoDB Port at displayed 27017 and click Save.
report.reason: Works as intended: Port is a required field, and the placeholder 27017 is only a hint, not a value. Saving with it empty is missing required input, so the form shows an error; entering the port fixes it.

explanation: Declaring a control ineffective or a hidden state unrecoverable without completing its confirmation or using the available global recovery action. Reviewed examples include a permission confirmation before drilling down and Reset all filters restoring a hidden card.
verificationGuidance: Inspect dialogs and page-level reset controls after the action.
Complete the confirmation or recovery and verify the resulting state.
Distinguish an extra required step from a control that fails after the complete supported workflow.

report.name: Selecting 'Granular' in data permissions does nothing
report.summary: Selecting 'Granular' in data permissions does nothing.
report.expected: Choosing Granular opens the table-level permissions for that group/database (e.g. /admin/permissions/data/group/4/database/1), where each table's access can be set.
report.actual: The popover closes, the URL stays /admin/permissions/data/group/4 (or /database/1), and the cell still shows 'Query builder only'. Opening /admin/permissions/data/group/4/database/1 directly works, so only the navigation from the option is broken. Same thing happens from the database-focused view.
reproSteps: Log in as admin, create a group 'Marketing' in People > Groups
Go to /admin/permissions/data/group/<marketing id>
Click the Create queries dropdown for Sample Database
Click 'Granular'
Note that nothing changes and you stay on the database list
report.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: choosing Granular shows a 'Limit access even though All Users has greater access?' confirmation, and confirming opens the table-level view.

explanation: Reading a save confirmation about one group’s configured permission as a statement about a user’s total effective access. Greater access through another group can remain in effect and may already have been explained by an earlier warning.
verificationGuidance: Separate the edited group’s setting from the union of the actor’s group permissions.
Read preceding inherited-access warnings and verify effective access with the actor before claiming the save dialog revoked it.

report.name: Save confirmation contradicts inherited data access warning
report.summary: Save confirmation contradicts inherited data access warning.
report.expected: The save confirmation should accurately describe the group's restriction without implying that members lose their greater inherited All Users access.
report.actual: The initial warning says All Users higher access overrides this setting, but Save permissions says 'QA People 0702 will not be able to use the query builder or write native queries for Sample Database.'
reproSteps: As administrator, use a custom group with a member and Query builder and native access to Sample Database; leave All Users with Query builder and native access.
In Admin Permissions Data, select that group and set Sample Database Create queries to No.
Observe the warning that All Users has greater access and will override this setting; click Revoke access.
Click Save changes and read the Save permissions confirmation.
report.reason: Works as intended: the save dialog describes the group's own permission setting, and All Users' greater access was already flagged in the earlier warning.

explanation: Expecting half of a composite credential to persist when clearing its key or value intentionally removes the whole unusable credential. The pair’s lifecycle differs from unrelated independently editable fields.
verificationGuidance: Check the credential schema and how empty key/value pairs serialize.
Test whether an intact valid pair persists and distinguish pair deletion from unintended loss of a complete credential.

report.name: Clearing either field of a saved webhook API key erases both
report.summary: Clearing either field of a saved webhook API key erases both.
report.expected: Reject a missing header key or preserve the unchanged Value; do not silently erase it.
report.actual: Save succeeds and both Key and Value reopen empty, although only Key was cleared. The readback AI assertion confirmed both fields are empty.
reproSteps: Create a disposable webhook with name, description and valid-format URL.
Select API Key authentication, Header, Key X-QA-Edge and Value edge-value; save.
Reopen and confirm both fields persisted.
Clear only Key, save and reopen.
report.reason: Works as intended: an API key needs both its key and its value to be valid, so clearing either field drops the whole credential.
